description: A terminal UI for tshark, inspired by Wireshark

summary.one_liner: Termshark is a terminal user interface for tshark, the command-line packet analyzer, inspired by Wireshark.
summary.what_it_does: Termshark opens pcap files or sniffs live network interfaces through tshark and shows the packets in a terminal UI. It applies Wireshark display filters to pcaps or live captures. It can reassemble and inspect TCP and UDP flows and view network conversations by protocol. The README also says it can copy ranges of packets to the clipboard from the terminal. Version 2.4 adds packet search and profiles for colors and columns. It is written in Go and is distributed as a single executable.
use_cases: inspect a pcap file on a remote machine over ssh
capture packets on a network interface from the terminal
filter packet captures with Wireshark display filters
follow TCP or UDP streams in a terminal
copy packet ranges to the clipboard
how_to_run: Ensure tshark (version 1.10.2 or higher) is in your PATH
notable: Terminal-based front end for tshark, so Wireshark-style analysis works over ssh on remote machines
Compiles to a single executable with downloads for Linux, macOS, BSD, Android (termux) and Windows
Packet search and color/column profiles added in v2.4
Uses Wireshark display filter syntax for pcaps and live captures
caveats: Requires tshark to be installed and in PATH; termshark does not do packet analysis on its own
Only exposes part of tshark's features; the README says many more are not yet exposed
Live capture requires that tshark is permitted to sniff on the interface
